response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to evaluate the security-critical OAuth flow addition, error handling, and test coverage.

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 423,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "safe_urlopen exception not caught, 500 errors on transient GitHub OAuth failures",
      "body": "OAuthLoginView's try/except wraps safe_urlread and parse_qsl, but the preceding safe_urlopen call to GitHub's OAuth access token endpoint is outside the try block. If GitHub's endpoint is unreachable, times out, or returns a non-2xx status, safe_urlopen raises and the user receives a 500 error rather than the graceful 'Invalid installation request.' page. Move safe_urlopen inside the try block so transient GitHub outages don't break all installations."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 502,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "KeyError risk on integration.metadata['sender'] when sender is absent",
      "body": "The user-mismatch check does integration.metadata['sender']['login'], which raises KeyError if 'sender' is missing from the metadata. build_integration only sets metadata['sender'] if state.get('sender') is truthy, so integrations created via build_integration directly (e.g., when the webhook hasn't arrived in time) lack this key. The result is a 500 error instead of the intended graceful error page. Use safe access: integration.metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login')."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 408,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OAuth authorize URL built with raw f-string instead of URL-encoded parameters",
      "body": "The redirect URL is constructed with f-string concatenation: f'{ghip.get_oauth_authorize_url()}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}'. If any value contains URL-special characters (&, =, %, ?, #, etc.) the URL is malformed. While current values appear URL-safe, this is fragile. Use urllib.parse.urlencode for robust URL construction."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py",
      "line": 481,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "TOCTOU race allows user-mismatch check to be bypassed when webhook is delayed",
      "body": "The user-mismatch check runs only if the Integration record already exists (which is created by the GitHub installation webhook). If the webhook hasn't been processed by the time the user reaches GitHubInstallation, Integration.DoesNotExist is raised and pipeline.next_step() runs without verifying the sender. build_integration then creates the Integration using only GitHub's installation API (which doesn't include the sender field), bypassing the check. The webhook typically arrives within seconds, but if delayed or skipped, an attacker who tricks a victim into completing OAuth can complete the integration in their own Sentry org using the victim's GitHub credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py",
      "line": 379,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "test_installation_not_found never starts a pipeline, assertion cannot pass",
      "body": "The test issues two GETs to self.setup_path but never visits self.init_path to start the pipeline. PipelineAdvancerView will not find a pipeline in progress for either GET and will fall through to redirect to '/' with 'Invalid request' (added via messages.add_message), returning a 302 whose body does not contain 'Invalid installation request.'. The test as written cannot reach OAuthLoginView's state-mismatch error path. To exercise that path the test must first visit self.init_path (starting the pipeline with the default signature) before calling self.setup_path with a non-matching state."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py",
      "line": 1,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Missing test coverage for several documented OAuth failure modes",
      "body": "The PR description lists three failure modes that lack explicit coverage: (1) state parameter mismatch, (2) GitHub rejecting the OAuth code (wrong or reused), (3) GitHub's /user endpoint not returning 'login'. The only failure case tested is the user mismatch. Tests for state mismatch (once test_installation_not_found is fixed), reused/invalid codes, /user error responses, and missing 'login' would help lock in the new validation behavior."
    }
  ]
}
```

findings.title: safe_urlopen exception not caught, 500 errors on transient GitHub OAuth failures
findings.body: OAuthLoginView's try/except wraps safe_urlread and parse_qsl, but the preceding safe_urlopen call to GitHub's OAuth access token endpoint is outside the try block. If GitHub's endpoint is unreachable, times out, or returns a non-2xx status, safe_urlopen raises and the user receives a 500 error rather than the graceful 'Invalid installation request.' page. Move safe_urlopen inside the try block so transient GitHub outages don't break all installations.

findings.title: KeyError risk on integration.metadata['sender'] when sender is absent
findings.body: The user-mismatch check does integration.metadata['sender']['login'], which raises KeyError if 'sender' is missing from the metadata. build_integration only sets metadata['sender'] if state.get('sender') is truthy, so integrations created via build_integration directly (e.g., when the webhook hasn't arrived in time) lack this key. The result is a 500 error instead of the intended graceful error page. Use safe access: integration.metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login').

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL built with raw f-string instead of URL-encoded parameters
findings.body: The redirect URL is constructed with f-string concatenation: f'{ghip.get_oauth_authorize_url()}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}'. If any value contains URL-special characters (&, =, %, ?, #, etc.) the URL is malformed. While current values appear URL-safe, this is fragile. Use urllib.parse.urlencode for robust URL construction.

findings.title: TOCTOU race allows user-mismatch check to be bypassed when webhook is delayed
findings.body: The user-mismatch check runs only if the Integration record already exists (which is created by the GitHub installation webhook). If the webhook hasn't been processed by the time the user reaches GitHubInstallation, Integration.DoesNotExist is raised and pipeline.next_step() runs without verifying the sender. build_integration then creates the Integration using only GitHub's installation API (which doesn't include the sender field), bypassing the check. The webhook typically arrives within seconds, but if delayed or skipped, an attacker who tricks a victim into completing OAuth can complete the integration in their own Sentry org using the victim's GitHub credentials.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found never starts a pipeline, assertion cannot pass
findings.body: The test issues two GETs to self.setup_path but never visits self.init_path to start the pipeline. PipelineAdvancerView will not find a pipeline in progress for either GET and will fall through to redirect to '/' with 'Invalid request' (added via messages.add_message), returning a 302 whose body does not contain 'Invalid installation request.'. The test as written cannot reach OAuthLoginView's state-mismatch error path. To exercise that path the test must first visit self.init_path (starting the pipeline with the default signature) before calling self.setup_path with a non-matching state.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for several documented OAuth failure modes
findings.body: The PR description lists three failure modes that lack explicit coverage: (1) state parameter mismatch, (2) GitHub rejecting the OAuth code (wrong or reused), (3) GitHub's /user endpoint not returning 'login'. The only failure case tested is the user mismatch. Tests for state mismatch (once test_installation_not_found is fixed), reused/invalid codes, /user error responses, and missing 'login' would help lock in the new validation behavior.
